checks.label: Same-seed restoration adds work on independent aggregates without replacing local work; repeated import is idempotent.
Equivalent operation objects with different property order remain one immutable journal entry.
A divergent seed is rejected before any write or state change, even when adoption is requested on a nonempty journal.
Only an explicitly requested adoption can attach a browser with no local operations to a different seed.
An existing ID with changed content rejects the entire incoming batch before its otherwise-valid new operation is written.
Two different operations with the same ID inside one packet are rejected without partial restoration.
Concurrent registry edits converge deterministically while preserving the rejected operation in both journals.
Browser backup round trip preserves the journal and detects changed content before any restoration.
A default browser backup restores into an isolated SQLite journal, survives reopening and restores additively into another browser.
Availability, in-flight writes, new edits and confirmed persistence have distinct truthful statuses.
A malformed success acknowledgement cannot claim persistence; rereading the committed journal recovers without duplicate entries.
A page claiming completion before the advertised cursor is rejected before merging a truncated journal.
A changed service identity blocks automatic continuation and preserves new local work.
A storage failure remains labelled memory-only until a separately confirmed service write exists.
Confirmed journal storage and a rejected business edit remain distinct when two registry revisions conflict.
Two real application windows preserve an unsaved fleet form and reject its stale revision without overwriting the first edit.
A project selection from another window preserves the current screen, tab and editor target, and saving still updates the original dossier.
The visible save indicator reports memory-only retention when browser storage is unavailable.
The continuity drawer and footer display saved-on-tower only after the actual repository acknowledgement returns.
A project created through the actual form survives browser backup, SQLite restoration and replay with its stage and empty geometry intact.

scope: Isolated JSDOM contexts, actual WorkshopStore, browser backup validator and SQLite repository. Temporary SQLite database only; no browser engine, socket or physical operation.
